subject: AWS Marketplace listing — procurement checklist & product page copy
messages:
From: Emily Torres <etorres@acme-analytics.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood-inference.com
Date: Mon, 6 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: AWS Marketplace listing — procurement checklist & sample copy

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the intro earlier. We're starting the procurement review for any new marketplace listings and I wanted to get a couple of things clarified before we lock in a date for the marketplace team to accept the listing. High level Qs below — can you confirm or point me at where to get definitive evidence?

1) Compliance/evidence: Do you have a SOC 2 Type II report, and do you publish an audit evidence package or a portal where we can pull the report?
2) Data residency & egress: Our legal requires specifics on where inference data is processed and any egress controls (region, retention, logs).
3) PCI/PHI: Do you support customers with PCI or PHI workloads on the hosted offering, and if so, what are the constraints?
4) Pricing & billing: What are your standard AWS Marketplace SKUs or pricing tiers (metered vs listing price)? Any common footnotes we should expect in procurement?
5) SSO/SSO provisioning: Do you support SCIM/Okta provisioning for self-serve seats (if applicable)?
6) Product page copy: We have a short product page draft and a hero claim that references latency and cost-savings — procurement wants the evidence that supports those claims or guidance on how to phrase them to avoid legal flagging.

If it's easier, we can take a 30-minute call — happy to propose times tomorrow.

Thanks,
Emily Torres
Procurement Lead, Acme Analytics

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood-inference.com>
To: Emily Torres <etorres@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>

Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace listing — procurement checklist & sample copy

Emily — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and then I've attached a working draft of the product page copy so you can see the exact wording we're proposing. If helpful, we can walk through on a 30-min call; times at the bottom.

- SOC 2: We are SOC 2 Type II certified; we host the evidence package behind a secure portal for procurement/customer review (we'll send a secure link once NDA/portal access is agreed).
- Data residency & egress: Hosted runs in the selected AWS region(s) for the tenant. By default data is processed in-region; we offer VPC/private deployments for strict residency requirements. We retain logs per contract — standard 90-day token retention by default; custom retention available for Enterprise.
- PCI/PHI: Hosted API is generally not PCI certified by default for customers storing cardholder data; we support PHI workloads under private deployments and a contractual BAAs — will loop legal if you need specifics.
- Pricing & billing: We support both fixed listing SKUs and meter-based pricing. Attached is our recommended SKU mapping and a sample pricing table. Generally we call out metered token pricing and a separate dedicated-reserved capacity SKU for predictable throughput.
- SSO: SCIM + SSO via SAML/Okta is supported for company accounts; we can share the config doc.
- Product page claims: See attached doc with suggested alternate phrasing for latency & cost claims and the evidence we can provide (benchmarks + customer references).

Attachments: redwood_aws_listing_draft_v1.docx

Proposed times for a short call:
- Tue 9am PT / 12pm ET
- Tue 2pm PT / 5pm ET
- Wed 10am PT / 1pm ET

If any of the above needs deeper detail, I'll pull in Sean for SLA language or legal for BAAs.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood-inference.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood-inference.com>

Subject: Fwd: AWS Marketplace listing — procurement checklist & sample copy

Fwding Emily's procurement list — adding pricing specifics and suggested footnotes.

Alex / Marissa — see my suggested SKU mapping below (draft):
- "redwood-hosted-metered": list price + metered token consumption (recommended footnote: "Metered pricing billed monthly; average usage discounts subject to committed volume.")
- "redwood-dedicated-reserved": monthly committed capacity (recommended footnote: "Reserved capacity billed monthly; overage charged at metered rate.")
- Private/VPC: enterprise license + infra uplift (contracted)

Procurement often calls out the SLA and data-handling footnote. I recommend we avoid absolute latency claims on the product page — instead use percentile phrasing backed by our benchmark (e.g., "95th percentile < 250ms on common prompt shapes"). Make sure the listing includes a short link to our evidence binder rather than embedding raw numbers.

I'll attach the Q4 pricing table for ACME to give them a sense of tiers.

Attachment: pricing_table_q4.csv

Kimberly Park
Head of GTM Pricing

Adding co-sell and field enablement notes. For the product page hero we should avoid specific % cost savings unless we have a public case study with a named customer. Suggested hero option: "High-throughput, production-ready LLM inference for engineering teams — predictable latency and cost controls."

Suggested bullets on product page:
- "Optimized GPU runtime with batching & caching for lower per-token costs"
- "SLA-backed availability & reserved capacity options"
- "Flexible deployment: hosted, dedicated, private (VPC)"

If ACME wants customer proof, we can offer a non-confidential usage vignette (e.g., "reduced inference spend by ~30% vs baseline when adopting reserved pools and caching") and point them to the evidence binder. Also recommend we include a short 'procurement notes' block near billing that links to the pricing table and includes the procurement contact and DocuSign PO template.

Marissa Cole
Partner & Field GTM

Answers (short):
1) SOC 2: Yes — SOC 2 Type II. We'll provision a secure evidence link and temporary portal access for your procurement/legal reviewer (requires a short NDA).
2) Data residency & egress: Hosted runs in-customer-region by default. We support VPC/private deployments for stricter residency and can enumerate retention options in contract.
3) PCI/PHI: We support PHI on Private deployments with BAAs; PCI use-cases vary — recommend Private for cardholder workflows.
4) Pricing & billing: See attached pricing_table_q4.csv — we support both metered and SKU pricing. Recommended marketplace pattern is to list a metered SKU and offer reserved capacity as a private SKU to simplify procurement.
5) SSO/SSO provisioning: SCIM + SAML/Okta supported; will share the integration doc after call.
6) Product page claims: See attached redwood_aws_listing_draft_v1.docx with revised hero and a short procurement notes block. We recommend using percentile latency phrasing (e.g., "95th percentile < 250ms for common prompt shapes") and a generic cost vignette instead of absolute % savings unless we link to a public case study.

Attachments included: redwood_aws_listing_draft_v1.docx; pricing_table_q4.csv; po_template_redwood.pdf (DocuSign-friendly PO template).
